question: Does preserving the three reference descriptors as a set, instead of averaging them, rank every consumed PV28 query view above both fixed cross-family controls?

predecessor.single_change: Keep the same descriptors and frozen images but score each query by its maximum cosine to any reference memory member instead of cosine to their averaged prototype.

descriptor.feature: The unchanged concatenated exact-bbox and 1.5x-context DINOv2 CLS descriptor.
descriptor.memory: Retain all three normalized descriptors without averaging.
descriptor.score: Maximum cosine similarity to any frozen reference member.

evaluation.decision_gate: All six positive-versus-negative nearest-member score comparisons must be strictly ordered correctly; no absolute threshold or margin is fitted.
evaluation.negative_authority: The two queries come from another physical scan family and cannot contain exact PV28; same-scene sibling rejection remains untested.

literature_motivation.use: A long-term object memory should preserve viewpoint-specific observation structure rather than collapse incompatible views into one mean.

forbidden_after_freeze: change features, crop scales, images, model, number of memory members or ranking gate
choose a member using query truth or discard a weak reference
fit an absolute threshold or margin from these scores
claim consumed cross-family ranking as fresh or same-scene confirmation
claim_boundary: This consumed Development test can establish only whether nearest-member object-context memory contains cross-family-separable PV28 signal under privileged target boxes. It cannot establish same-scene sibling rejection, open-set calibration, raw-camera initial binding, named entrance, ownership, access, traversability, waypoint, arrival, handoff, deployment, benefit, reliability or safety.
